title: Chicken Tender Plate with Fries, Coleslaw and Texas Toast
summary: Buttermilk-marinated chicken tenders in a flaky, lightly spiced flour coat, served as a full plate with seasoned frozen fries, a crunchy lemony coleslaw and garlic-butter Texas toast. A tangy mayo-ketchup dipping sauce goes on the side.
notes: Video: 'The Ultimate Chicken Tender Plate At Home' on the Joshua Weissman Recipes channel (UCUAg71CJEvFdOnujmep1Svw). Written recipe for the same dish: https://www.joshuaweissman.com/recipes/the-ultimate-chicken-tender-plate-at-home-recipe (serves 6, prep 30 min, cook 30 min; the marinade rest of 20 minutes to overnight is not included). He serves tenders, fries, coleslaw and Texas toast together as one plate, so they are one recipe here. The video states every amount for the marinade, dredge, fry seasoning, coleslaw, toast butter and sauce, and the 2 lb of tenders. From the written recipe: 6 slices of thick-cut white bread (the video only says two or three halves per person), 1/2 cup (10 g) parsley, 1 bag of frozen fries, and 1/2 tsp dried thyme in the fry seasoning (the captions read 'A/ teaspoon'). Our estimates: frozen fries bag 26 oz (737 g); Texas toast slice 40 g; lemon zest 1 Tbsp for one lemon; 1/2 tsp kosher salt for the 'generous pinch' on the cabbage (some leaves with the squeezed-out water, so this may overstate) and 1/4 tsp for the 'pinch of salt to taste'. Ranges: chives 1-2 Tbsp, we use 1. House rules applied: the buttermilk marinade is a liquid marinade that is drained off before dredging, so it is not counted (this leaves out the buttermilk and salt that cling to the tenders, so sodium is somewhat understated); the dredge is counted at 25%; the fry seasoning is counted at half, because he tosses the fries with it but does not say how much of the batch goes on; absorbed frying oil is 10% of the raw weight of the fried tenders (with counted dredge) and of the fries, shown in each line's amount_note; the 3 quarts of frying oil are not counted. The dipping sauce ('OG sauce', about 1,600 kcal for the batch, mostly the 1 cup of mayonnaise) is served on the side in ramekins and is not counted. Black pepper 'to taste' in the coleslaw is not counted. All of the toast butter (1/2 cup) is counted; he says to brush thinly, so some may be left in the pan. Optional items are counted only because he adds them on camera (house rule 11): MSG and chives in the coleslaw, parsley on the toast, and the fry seasoning. The optional Sriracha is in the side sauce, so it is excluded anyway. Marinating: at least 20 minutes, ideally overnight (up to 2 days), not in prep_minutes. Chicken tenders use USDA breast meat only, raw, as a proxy; frozen fries use USDA frozen french fries, unprepared; Dijon uses the nearest USDA mustard (see new_h3.csv).

steps.text: Marinade: whisk the buttermilk with the salt, sugar, MSG, garlic powder, onion powder, smoked paprika and cayenne until the spices are evenly mixed.
Check each tender for the white tendon. Slide a sharp knife under it to loosen it, grip the end with a paper towel, hook a fork under it and pull it out. A tender that tears in two is fine.
Put the tenders in the marinade and massage so every surface is coated and none stick together. Cover and refrigerate at least 20 minutes, ideally overnight (up to 2 days).
Dredge: whisk the flour with the salt, MSG, garlic and onion powders, black pepper, smoked paprika, cayenne and the dried thyme (crushed between your fingers) until uniform.
Fry seasoning (optional): whisk together the bouillon powder, smoked paprika, cayenne, garlic powder, cumin, black pepper, salt, sugar and thyme.

Coleslaw: halve and core a medium-small green cabbage and shave it as thinly as you can, about 4 cups. Massage with a generous pinch of salt until it weeps, let it sit a minute or two, then wring it out over the sink and move it to a clean bowl.

Add the grated carrot, lemon zest, mayonnaise, Dijon, sugar, MSG, black pepper, a pinch of salt and the cider vinegar, and toss until fully coated. Fold in the chives if using. Dress it close to serving.
Texas toast: melt the butter in a small saucepan over medium heat, take it off the heat, and stir in the garlic and salt. Let it steep for 20-30 seconds.
Brush each slice of thick white bread thinly on both sides with the garlic butter and bake at 375°F for 10-12 minutes. Finish with parsley if you like and keep warm (or rewarm in foil).
Dipping sauce: whisk the mayonnaise, ketchup, Dijon, Worcestershire, vinegar, garlic powder, MSG and optional Sriracha with a little salt and pepper. Serve it on the side.

Use one hand for wet and one for dry. Flick some marinade into the dredge two times and toss, to make small clumps. Lift each tender from the marinade, press and toss it in the dredge until fully covered, shake off the excess and set it on a tray. Work two or three at a time.

Heat about 3 quarts of vegetable oil to 350°F in a large pot filled a little over halfway. Fry the frozen fries in batches until the bubbling slows and they are golden and crisp, then toss them straight away with the fry seasoning.
Fry the tenders in batches of three or four, laying them in away from you, until golden, the bubbling has slowed and the inside reads 165°F.
Plate a pile of fries with the tenders, coleslaw and sauce in ramekins, and the Texas toast cut in half on the diagonal.
